page: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In synthetic CPU benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core CPU performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng multi-core score of 99,821.78. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average performance, with read-only cached small block bandwidth at 3,492.82 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 65.88 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark physics tests show average to strong capabilities.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the integrated 1600 GB NVMe SSD, this instance is configured for memory-intensive and database workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance for database operations, Redis caching, and medium-scale LLM inference, where it achieves 20.46 tokens/sec for text generation on a 7B model. The lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training, but the high memory capacity and local NVMe storage make it suitable for memory-optimized databases, data processing pipelines, and web serving environments.
